title: 2008 HMMT November General Round 2 Problem 2
statement: Joe B. then places a white king in the opposite corner of the board. How many total ways can he place one black bishop and one white bishop so that neither checks the king of the opposite color?

solutions.text: 876 Observe that either both bishops are on the diagonal containing both kings or neither are. If both are on the diagonal, each of the \(\binom{4}{2}=6\) choices of pairs of squares yields one possible configuration, so there are 6 possibilities in this case. Off the diagonal, any pair of locations works, giving \(30 \cdot 29=870\) possibilities in this case. Summing, we obtain \(870+6=876\) total possibilities.
